summary: SDK connection-starvation + aggressive retry backoff misconfiguration causing apparent inference token delivery delays
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightLedger reports intermittent long-tail token delivery delays from Redwood API during high-concurrency batch scoring. Responses from the service appear normal in traces (sub-200ms server processing) but customer-observed end-to-end latency spikes to multiple seconds on a subset of requests.

Impact:
- Several BrightLedger production endpoints (dedicated pool) seeing 5-10% of user requests delayed by 2-8s during peak windows.
- Customer experienced increased user-facing timeouts and retry storms within their app.

Environment:
- Dedicated capacity, prod us-east region
- BrightLedger uses redwood-js-sdk v1.6.2 with default client configuration in a horizontally scaled Node.js service.
- Typical concurrency: 60-120 parallel inference requests per instance (small requests, many concurrent).

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start 100 parallel small-batch (1-4 prompts) scoring requests using redwood-js-sdk default client config.
2) Observe that most requests return in ~200ms, but ~5-10% experience 2-8s latency.
3) Enabling verbose SDK debug logs shows requests queued in SDK prior to network send.

Observed behavior:
- Server traces show request handled in ~120-220ms.
- SDK logs show enqueue/wait events with exponential backoff attempts and long per-request wait times before TCP send.
- No 5xx from Redwood, few 429s noted earlier in week (likely related to the same config).

Expected behavior:
- Requests either be sent immediately or retried quickly; not accumulate multi-second client-side queuing when server responds fast.

Logs/snippets (customer):
[2026-03-09T14:12:03.153Z] SDK DEBUG enqueue request id=cb4f3
[2026-03-09T14:12:03.157Z] HTTP SEND request id=cb4f3 -> /v1/generate (no backoff)
[2026-03-09T14:12:05.672Z] SDK DEBUG retry backoff enter request id=cb4f7 delay=5000ms attempt=2
[2026-03-09T14:12:07.007Z] HTTP RESPONSE request id=cb4f3 status=200 time=145ms
[2026-03-09T14:12:09.009Z] SDK DEBUG dequeue request id=cb4f7 (waited=7387ms)

Notes: logs indicate request cb4f7 did not hit network for ~7s despite overall low server latency for other requests.

Attachments: customer provided SDK debug traces and a short Flamegraph showing Node event-loop idle time while requests awaited SDK queue slot.

Recommended immediate workaround for customer:
- Increase SDK connection pool and concurrent send slots from default (v1.6.2 defaults to poolSize=8) to poolSize=40 for their concurrency pattern.
- Reduce client max_backoff_ms from 60000 to 5000 to avoid multi-second queuing during transient throttling.
- Instrument SDK debug metrics to emit queue_length and avg_wait_ms per instance.

Follow-ups required:
- Engineering review to adjust SDK defaults or add heuristic warnings when init detects high concurrency vs. small pool size.
- Add an observability metric in platform to detect high client-side queuing reported by SDK telemetry.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Asha Patel (Support): Opened ticket after CS handoff from account team. Collected initial SDK traces and environment details from BrightLedger. Escalated to SRE/Eng.
2026-03-10 - BrightLedger (Customer): Provided reproduction harness and logs. Confirmed they run 60-120 concurrent scoring requests per instance. Asked for best-practice config.

2026-03-11 - Diego Martinez (SRE): Initial investigation shows client-side queuing in SDK. Server traces correlate that the service answered quickly for most requests. Suspect small connection pool and amplified retry backoff. Assigned INT-4129 to prototype mitigations.

2026-03-11 - Engineering (Investigator): Reproduced locally with redwood-js-sdk v1.6.2. Default poolSize=8 leads to queued requests under 100 concurrent clients. After increasing poolSize to 40 and capping max_backoff_ms to 5s, tails drop to <1%.

2026-03-12 - BrightLedger (Customer): Applied recommended workaround (poolSize=40, max_backoff_ms=5000). Confirmed 95th/99th percentile improved and user-facing timeouts resolved. Asked about permanent fix and SDK release timeline.
investigation:
Timeline and findings:
- 2026-03-10 09:00 UTC: Customer reported issue.
- Reproduced in our lab using the customer's harness. With default SDK settings (poolSize=8, exponential backoff max=60s), concurrent requests above pool size cause the SDK to serialize outgoing HTTP sends behind a fixed-size socket pool.
- When transient 429s occur (observed earlier), the SDK's retry/backoff logic delays re-sends and holds queued requests for the backoff duration. Because queue slots are limited, new requests pile up in the SDK queue rather than being sent or failing fast. That creates the illusion of server slowness even when the server processes other requests quickly.
- Root cause: combination of (a) conservative default poolSize in SDK for Node.js, (b) large max_backoff_ms and no circuit-breaker for queued requests, and (c) customer workload pattern (many small, high-concurrency requests).
- Corroborating evidence: network traces show lack of outbound SYN until much later for delayed requests; server logs show corresponding requests handled quickly.
resolution:
Resolution and action items:
- Immediate: Advised BrightLedger to update SDK config to poolSize=40 and set max_backoff_ms=5000. Customer applied change and confirmed mitigation on 2026-03-12.
- Short-term dev fix: INT-4129 created to implement SDK client-side safeguards: emit warnings at init when estimated concurrency > poolSize * 2, add a hard cap on per-request queue wait (fail-fast after configurable threshold), and shorten default max_backoff_ms to 10s for v1.7.0.
- Long-term: PR github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3481 adds telemetry hooks for client-side queue length to the Console and runbook updates. Also update our docs with recommended pool sizing guidelines for high-concurrency dedicated deployments.
- Postmortem notes: not a server regression; misalignment between SDK defaults and certain dedicated customer workloads. Update alerts to detect client-side queueing signals so we can proactively advise customers.
post_actions: INT-4129: implement SDK warnings and fail-fast queue cap
Backport SDK patch to v1.6.x branch and release v1.6.3
Docs: add 'Sizing the client connection pool' guide under SDK best practices
Add client-queue-length metric to Redwood Console dashboard and alert when >100ms avg wait for >5min
